The core operator is the drawdown probability minimizer φ(w,m) which seeks to minimize P(τ_α < τ_d). This involves solving a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) variational inequality. The solution yields a feedback control π(w,m) that depends on current wealth w and running maximum m. The key insight is that π_t ∝ (c/r - W_t), meaning investment becomes more aggressive as wealth approaches the safe level c/r. This is structurally opposite to Kelly betting, which increases position size with wealth. The problem splits into regimes determined by the safe level and a critical threshold m*. The minimum drawdown probability in regime ii is expressed via Legendre duality of a controller-stopper problem’s value function. The mathematical structure supports a dual formulation where the optimal strategy is derived through variational inequalities rather than direct optimization. The failure mode arises when discrete approximations distort the continuous-time feedback structure, especially under lumpy withdrawals.
